newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall by lunch on liquidity concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall by lunch on liquidity concerns.

text.p: Thai stocks dropped sharply during the morning session on Friday as hopes of an IMF backed financial package evaporated and the market returned to consider fundamental economic and liquidity concerns, analysts said.
The SET index lost 15.10 points or 2.30 percent to 641.18. The SET 50 dropped 1.40 points or 2.82 percent to 48.28. Turnover was 2.65 billion baht.

"I think Bangkok Bank raising deposit rates may have had some impact on the market because basically it confirms the liquidity crunch in the financial system," said Tom Paiboon, head of research at TISCO Plc.
Bangkok Bank Plc, the country's largest commercial lender, raised a range of fixed deposit rates by at least 75 basis points on Thursday.
Liquidity has become a concern as interbank lending has been around 15-20 percent since the baht was floated on July 2.
"We have not been very positive anyway on the market and think it has been driven up by sentiment not fundamentals of the economy, so given that I don't think the rally is sustainable," Paiboon said.

Hopes of an IMF or Japanese-sponsored financial package, which have driven the market higher this week, evaporated after Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said Thailand would not seek an aid package at this time.
With the market now returning to dwell on more fundamental economic concerns, which look gloomy in the short term, most key sectors were sold during the morning session, analysts said.
Siam Cement Plc dipped 28 baht to 482, BEC World Plc lost 22 to 238, Siam Commercial Bank Plc shed one to 119.
